post.caption: Iridium is named after a rainbow goddess. Iris was the Greek goddess of the rainbow. Iridium got its name because its salts show many colors. In 1803, Smithson Tennant found it in the leftovers of dissolved platinum. Other chemists had mistaken that black powder for graphite. In bulk, even aqua regia cannot dissolve iridium. Jewelers often harden platinum with a little iridium. A common alloy is 90 percent platinum and 10 percent iridium. For decades, the world's kilogram was a cylinder of that alloy. Its vault needs three keys held by three officials. That cylinder stopped defining the kilogram in 2019.
